record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Replace the algebraic framework of equivariant map algebras with an analytic one. For a Banach manifold X, a Banach algebra a, and a group Γ acting by automorphisms, develop the theory and representation theory of algebras of Γ-equivariant differentiable maps from X to a.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

(d) Analytic setting. Another interesting problem is to replace the algebraic setting by an analytic one. For example, let X be a Banach manifold, a a Banach algebra and consider equivariant differentiable maps X → a.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach manifold, let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a Banach algebra, and let $\Gamma$ be a group acting on $X$ by diffeomorphisms and on $\mathfrak{a}$ by continuous algebra automorphisms. Consider the algebra
$$\mathcal{M}_{\text{an}}(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma} = \{\,f : X \to \mathfrak{a} \mid f \text{ is differentiable and } f(\gamma\cdot x) = \gamma\cdot f(x) \text{ for all } \gamma\in\Gamma,\ x\in X\,\}$$
of $\Gamma$-equivariant differentiable maps from $X$ to $\mathfrak{a}$, equipped with pointwise multiplication.

Develop a structure theory and representation theory for these algebras analogous to the algebraic theory of equivariant map algebras $(\mathfrak{a}\otimes A)^{\Gamma}$ (where $A$ is the coordinate ring of an affine scheme $X$ with $\Gamma$ acting on both factors). In particular:

1. Classify the (topologically) irreducible finite-dimensional, or suitably continuous, representations of $\mathcal{M}_{\text{an}}(X,\mathfrak{a})^{\Gamma}$.
2. Describe extensions, evaluation representations, and Weyl-type modules in this analytic/Banach setting.
3. Determine to what extent the known parametrizations of irreducible representations in the algebraic equivariant map algebra setting carry over when $X$ is replaced by a Banach manifold and $\mathfrak{a}$ by a Banach algebra.
artifact.status_search_result: No published work was located that develops a representation theory of equivariant map algebras in the proposed analytic Banach setting (Banach manifold $X$, Banach algebra $\mathfrak{a}$, group $\Gamma$ acting by automorphisms). Existing literature treats either the algebraic theory of equivariant map algebras or unrelated analytic problems concerning equivariant maps (e.g., harmonic maps, normal forms). The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Normal form of equivariant maps in infinite dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Local normal form theorems for smooth equivariant maps between infinite-dimensional manifolds (Banach/Fréchet).
status_evidence.claim: Analytic equivariant maps are studied in differential geometry but not in the representation-theoretic framework of equivariant map algebras.

status_evidence.title: Equivariant harmonic maps depend real analytically on the representation
status_evidence.snippet: Real analytic dependence of equivariant harmonic maps; mapping spaces as Banach manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Related analytic equivariant frameworks exist but do not address representation theory of equivariant map algebras over Banach algebras.
